task_instance: Bind an existing DPDK app's port id to a doca_dev via doca_dpdk_port_probe/doca_dpdk_port_as_dev and add a DOCA Flow steering rule on it (the skill's canonical worked example), verified by building/running against the installed DOCA DPDK Bridge and DPDK.
blocker_detail: The skill's compatibility section requires the DOCA SDK installed at /opt/mellanox/doca plus a separate DPDK install, 'with a BlueField DPU or ConnectX NIC attached'. This sandbox has neither: pkg-config --exists doca-dpdk-bridge and pkg-config --exists libdpdk both fail (exit 1), /opt/mellanox/doca does not exist, and lspci shows no Mellanox/ConnectX/BlueField hardware present. The bridge's entire surface (doca_dpdk_port_probe/doca_dpdk_port_as_dev binding a real DPDK rte_eth port id to a doca_dev, doca_dpdk_cap_is_rep_port_supported queries, mbuf<->doca_buf conversion, DOCA Flow steering on the bound port) is meaningless without a physical NVIDIA ConnectX NIC or BlueField DPU backing an actual PCIe device -- this is not a package that can simply be apt-installed or emulated; DOCA's kernel/userspace drivers bind to real NIC hardware. No installable software substitute exists in this runtime, so the core deliverable (bridging a real DPDK port to DOCA and installing a hardware-offloaded flow rule) cannot be attempted, let alone verified.
evidence: cd into scratchpad work dir; ran: pkg-config --exists doca-dpdk-bridge -> exit 1; pkg-config --exists libdpdk -> exit 1; ls /opt/mellanox/doca -> 'No such file or directory'; lspci | grep -i mellanox -> no output; lspci | grep -i ConnectX -> no output. Confirms neither the DOCA SDK nor DPDK are installed, and no BlueField DPU / ConnectX NIC hardware is present in this VM, which the skill's own compatibility block lists as hard prerequisites.
